scientific_queries.note: Nested validation of the R79 triage rule, with threshold selection inside each outer fold.

subagent_note: None dispatched: the round overturns its own previous verdict by validating the threshold honestly.

design.inner: leave-one-out within the 122 training cells to select the threshold
design.threshold_rule: fixed in advance: among thresholds with precision >= 0.50 take the best recall; otherwise take the best precision
design.reported: precision and recall of the flagged set on the outer folds only

overturns: R79 concluded the rule was usable for triage because at threshold 0.2 it flagged 55% of cells and captured 94% of the never-benefiting ones; that threshold was read off the same LOO predictions, and honest inner selection collapses recall to 0.531 while flagging only 30% of cells
why: the R79 threshold captured the tail of one particular sample; the inner folds hold only about 31 positives, so the selected threshold itself varies widely (0.281-0.419)

line_status.R78: single features: AUC 0.63, below the 0.65 bar
line_status.R79: three features: AUC 0.79 but precision 0.50, claimed triage-only
line_status.R80: nested validation: recall 0.53 and precision 0.46, so not even triage
line_status.conclusion: advance identification of which cells to personalise is closed as not achievable on this resource

limits: 32 positives make every nested estimate noisy (precision CI roughly +/-0.16)
the threshold rule was fixed before running, which removes tuning freedom but may not be the best rule
retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim; no meta-learning or RSI

register_updates.C54: new and decisive: the triage rule fails nested validation
